findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed a missed handwashing opportunity with a staff member preparing food items. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were washed. Ensure staff is washing hands as needed.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed a coffee pot to be resting in hand sink. Discussed with PIC, pot was removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sinks are used solely for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handlers licenses to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, licenses will be acquired by staff. Ensure any food handling employee has completed the food handlers training within 30 days of employment. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager is present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the bottom of the sandwich prep cooler to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, cooler will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact areas are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at mop sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/replacing caulking as needed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: Observed a pizza cutter being stored in the chemical tubing above triple sink. Discussed with PIC and relocated cutter to an appropriate area. Ensure pizza cutter is stored in a dry, clean area where it will not get splash from warewashing. 
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-202.16: Observed multiple cardboard cutouts being used to hold utensils in shelves below back prep table in kitchen, and being used to hold single service condiments in the self serve area. Discussed with PIC. Ensure non absorbent materials are being used for facility surfaces.  
4-202.16: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Observed slushee machine to have some spillage under machine and also observed food splash near the soda syrup boxes in the back holding area. Discussed with PIC. Ensure facility is cleaned regularly. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be in need of cleaning:
1. The stand up shelving unit that holds large trays has food debris in the crevices of the unit. Clean the unit.
2. The shelf above the main pizza prep cooler (in kitchen) has food debris on the grates. Scale on shelf has debris. Clean the grates and scale.
3. The walk-in freezer in the kitchen has food spillage and box debris under the shelving units. Sweep and mop under shelving to maintain clean.
4. The reach-in customer cooler with subs has dust on the front vent (look down). Clean the vent of dust.
5. The area near the fryer and main pizza prep cooler in the kitchen has debris around the coving. Ensure equipment gets moved to remove debris when sweeping and mopping.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure above areas are maintained clean. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) A crack is observed in the counter behind the coffee pots. The crack is not easily cleanable but appears to be clean at this time. PIC instructed to repair/replace so as to ensure easily cleanable surfaces near the food and drink areas. As it does not appear that the crack is becoming worse, caulking the crack could allow for a smooth and easily cleanable surface that inspector would find acceptable. 2) The wall coving next to the mop sink is observed pulling away from the wall. PIC instructed to reseal to the wall and ensure that it remains in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. 

On arrival, three quarter pans were observed in the sanitizing sink of the three part sink. The concentration was measured at below 100 ppm Quat. Bottle indicates that this is not an effective concentration for sanitizing food contact surfaces. The solution was emptied and refilled fresh from the dispenser to register at 400 ppm Quat.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Sandwiches and salads with turkey/ham are observed with internal temperatures of 45-50 on the bottom shelf of the sandwich display in the center of the floor. A discussion with the PIC involving the cooler commenced and the items noted were discarded. Inspector will spot check the cooler in the future to verify its ability to maintain the bottom shelf's temperature. The other shelves on the stand all were at correct temperatures.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Multiple utensils are observed stored in a shelf at the right of the back wall under a counter, and the shelves are observed soiled with crumbs and an oily residue. The shelves and the utensils were cleaned during the inspection to correct.
